      Problem: Removal of newline="\n" parameter in write_text introduces platform-dependent line endings.; On Windows, Python's write_text() translates \n to \r\n by default. This causes generated shell scripts to have CRLF line endings, which leads to "bad interpreter" or "command not found" errors when executed in Linux environments (e.g., within Docker or GitHub Actions runners) because the shell sees the carriage return as part of the command or shebang path. Although _normalize_newlines ensuring internal \n, write_text() will still translate them upon writing if newline is not strictly set to "\n" or "".
      Confidence: avg 5.0
      Flagged by: google_gemini-3-flash-preview

  [6] File: scripts/render_validation_templates.py
      Problem: Platform-dependent line endings — removal of newline control breaks deterministic output on Windows.; Path.write_text() with default newline=None performs newline translation on Windows, converting \n to \r\n. Even though _normalize_newlines() normalizes content to Unix \n, writing without explicit newline="\" reverts to platform default on Windows, producing CRLF line endings in generated shell scripts. This can cause "bad interpreter" errors (e.g., #!/usr/bin/env bash\r) when scripts are executed on Unix-like systems or in TAP consumers expecting LF. The repository requires deterministic output regardless of runner OS.; Evidence: The function _normalize_newlines (lines 132-136) normalizes all line endings to \n and ensures a trailing newline. The write_text call at line 367 removed the explicit newline="\n" parameter that previously preserved these LF endings on all platforms. In Python's text mode (Windows), omitting newline causes \n → \r\n translation. The codebase targets Python 3.12 in CI; Path.write_text gained the newline parameter in Python 3.10, so using it directly excluded <3.10, but removing it entirely reintroduces Windows-specific line-ending corruption.; HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS:
      Confidence: avg 4.0
      Flagged by: stepfun_step-3_5-flash

      Problem: Potential UndefinedError if 'slots' or 'slots.canary_tools' is missing.; The template assumes 'slots.canary_tools' is always present in the Jinja2 context. If a manifest family uses this shared template but does not populate the 'canary_tools' slot, rendering will fail with an UndefinedError. While the previous iteration also used 'slots.canary_tools' in a loop (which would just be an empty loop if missing), the new length calculation 'slots.canary_tools | length' is more likely to trigger an error depending on the Jinja2 environment configuration (StrictUndefined is used in scripts/render_validation_templates.py).; HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS:
